stories.title: The final Disrupt Stage lineup: Three days of conversations you won’t hear anywhere outside of TechCrunch Disrupt 2026
stories.simple_summary: TechCrunch is announcing speakers for a tech conference in 2026 and offering discounts on tickets.
stories.why_it_matters: This is only relevant if you want to attend a tech conference — nothing you need to act on otherwise.

stories.title: SpaceX renaming AI unit SpaceXSI amid Trump rebranding push
stories.simple_summary: SpaceX is renaming its AI division as part of changes happening with the new administration.
stories.why_it_matters: This is a business name change at a space company — it doesn't affect ordinary people or small businesses.

stories.title: Can Safeworld convince people that GenAI robots won’t hurt them?
stories.simple_summary: A company called Safeworld is working on AI robots and trying to make sure they're safe and won't harm people.
stories.why_it_matters: This matters only if you work in manufacturing or will use robots in the future — most small businesses don't need to worry about this yet.

stories.title: ‘Clearly not working’: Sam Altman hits AI industry over political spending
stories.simple_summary: The leader of a major AI company is criticizing other AI companies for spending money on political campaigns.
stories.why_it_matters: This is mostly relevant to investors and people interested in politics — not something that affects how you'd use AI.

stories.title: Trump chooses top spy boss to run new AI taskforce
stories.simple_summary: The government is creating a new team to oversee AI, and a high-ranking intelligence official has been chosen to lead it.
stories.why_it_matters: This means the government is paying attention to AI, which could lead to new rules in the future that might affect businesses.

stories.title: Our minds aren’t equipped to handle AI
stories.simple_summary: Experts are discussing whether human brains are actually ready to understand and use AI the way it's being developed.
stories.why_it_matters: This is a philosophical discussion among academics — it doesn't change how AI works or how you'd use it today.

stories.title: AI is being taught how to do your job. Will artificial intelligence replace us, or just change the way we work?
stories.simple_summary: AI is learning to do tasks that people do at work, and experts are debating whether it will replace workers or just change their jobs.
stories.why_it_matters: This matters to anyone with employees — it's worth thinking about how AI might change the work in your business over time.

stories.title: Google froze its open source bug bounty program due to a ‘significant rise’ in AI submissions
stories.simple_summary: Google paused a program where people report security problems because too many reports were being generated by AI instead of real people.
stories.why_it_matters: This is mostly a tech industry issue — it shows that AI-generated content is sometimes low quality and clutters up useful work.

stories.title: Can ‘super intelligence’ and a non-binding safety pact solve AI’s image problem?
stories.simple_summary: There are discussions about rebranding AI and creating safety agreements to improve AI's reputation.
stories.why_it_matters: This is mainly about PR and politics in the tech industry — it doesn't change how AI actually works.

stories.title: Trump names national intelligence chief Jay Clayton as new AI czar
stories.simple_summary: The government has appointed a spy agency leader to oversee a new national AI task force.
stories.why_it_matters: This means the government is taking AI seriously enough to put leadership in place — it could lead to new regulations affecting businesses.

stories.title: AI is evolving rapidly. Is it a new form of life?
stories.source: ABC News & Headlines – Australian Broadcasting Corporation
stories.simple_summary: People are debating whether rapidly advancing AI should be considered a new form of life.
stories.why_it_matters: This is a philosophical and scientific debate — it doesn't change anything about how AI works today.

stories.title: NJ’s former Lt Gov is using AI to say he’s innocent of sexual harassment
stories.simple_summary: A former government official who resigned over harassment allegations is using AI technology to try to defend himself in interviews.
stories.why_it_matters: This shows AI is being used to spread messages, which is something to be aware of when you see information online — but it doesn't affect your business operations.
